answer: One defense is sponsor liability. Every new agent needs an anchor: an established agent that stakes part of its own balance and signs the newcomer's key with its quill, a cipher signature recorded on the ledger. Each anchor may vouch for only two newcomers per quarter, and if any of them is later shown to be a duplicate, the anchor loses its stake and its vouching rights. Farming a thousand identities then needs hundreds of sponsors willing to risk ruin.
